utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Good morning. Please be seated. We'll now resume the hearing. Have the accused brought in, please? (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like to say good morning to the interpreters. They are ready. Does everybody hear me? General Blaskic, do you hear? The Defence, the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I hear you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Good morning. Very well, I see it's Mr. Kehoe who is representing the Prosecution this morning. Mr. Kehoe, introduce the witness to us. It's going to be a protected witness, but it's a public hearing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Yes, that's correct. The next witness, whose pseudonym will be used, Mr. President, is Witness NN. The factual basis for this witness, Mr. President, will be directed, for the most part, to the village of Tulica and the attack in the village of Tulica in June of 1993. If I may illuminate the ELMO for one moment to place Tulica geographically, if I could ask the people in the booth to do that. The document on the ELMO is the document, my colleague, Mr. Harmon introduced yesterday, or maybe it was the day before yesterday, which is Exhibit 238 -- excuse me. We want the bottom half of that. We are now moving down the valley, Mr. President, and Your Honours, to the village of Tulica, which is the village in orange in the lower right-hand corner of Exhibit 238. Witness NN, Mr. President, Your Honours, will talk to some degree of some of the experiences and conflicts with the HVO in 1992 but, as I noted, the large part of his testimony will focus on the village of Tulica, and he will talk about the attack on the village of Tulica that commenced on the 12th of June, 1993. He will talk about how he came home to take a bath that day from the line. He was a soldier of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. He came back and the attack began in the village with shelling from the HVO locations and from the Serb or VRS locations, the armed forces of the Republic of Serbia. He will then talk about the infantry attack that surrounded the village with HVO soldiers and then when sabotage special units came in to essentially clean the village. Cleaning the village amounted to burning of houses, taking various individuals out, separating the women and children from men of military age. And then he will talk about the execution in front of him and around him of no fewer than seven Bosnian Muslim men, unarmed and defenceless. There will be some other information he will relate, Mr. President, and Your Honours, concerning looting that was taking place during this time period, in addition to the killings, the beatings that were taking place during this incident, and then he will talk about being taken with other Bosnian Muslim men to the Kiseljak barracks where he was, again, beaten, and then he was taken out to dig trenches thereafter. He will talk about numerous beatings and numerous individuals that were taken out of the Kiseljak barracks to dig trenches. He will talk about efforts on behalf of the HVO to avoid detection by the Red Cross by taking beaten prisoners out of the barracks to another location in the Kiseljak barracks. Essentially, Mr. President, that, in synopsis, will be the testimony of Witness NN. If we turn to the indictment, of course, these facts are covered by the persecution counts set forth in count 1. They are covered by the willful killing and causing serious injury counts set forth in counts 5 through 10. The facts will encompass counts 11 through 13, the destruction and plunder of property, and while we do have the designation of the village of Tulica and the destruction of religious institutions, that will be covered by a separate witness. So, in sum, Mr. President, the focus will be counts 1 through 13 and, if I may, much of the inhumane treatment that took place in counts 15 through 20; that inhumane treatment focusing on the Kiseljak barracks which is one of the prisons listed in paragraph 12. We mentioned at the outset, Mr. President, that Witness NN is a protected witness. There is face, name and voice distortion, and while after a few introductory paragraphs, if we could go into private session just for a few minutes to cover a few questions concerning his background -- and I say a few minutes -- just several questions, to cover some things in his background to prevent his identity, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. As regards to the summary, the Judges thank you. You have a very precise summary, and I ask you, Mr. Kehoe, that when the witness testifies, please do not have him repeat what he already said. The Judges understand what the witness is saying. You don't have to keep asking the witness to repeat himself. It's clear already. The second thing I would like to say is that we are going to have the witness brought in. Would you like the private session which will last for a few minutes take place immediately so we don't have to raise the blinds up and down, or will it be during his examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, it will be during his examination-in-chief shortly after I begin; however, it only need be a private session. It need not be a closed session. So I don't believe, Mr. President, that we need to raise and lower the blinds for those very few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Then we can have a private session. Registrar, please have the witness brought in, have the blinds lowered for the time it takes to bring the witness in, and then we will lift them once he has settled in. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you hear me now? First, we would like you to check your identity, that's on a document that the Registrar is going to give to you. Don't state your name, just look at it and nod. This is to check on your identity. Then he will give you a document which will be your solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. You have agreed to testify at the request of the Prosecution as part of the trial of the International Criminal Tribunal of the accused who is present in this courtroom; that is, General Blaskic who, at the time, was a Colonel. After a few brief questions, you will speak about the events of which the Prosecutor has given us the named points. If you forget some important details, important for the Prosecution, the Prosecutor will ask you further questions. After the Prosecutor, the Defence will have its turn to ask its questions. There are two lawyers; that is one of the lawyers of General Blaskic will ask questions and then the Judges will ask you questions at the end. Mr. Kehoe, please proceed. WITNESS NN Examined by MR. KEHOE

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness NN.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I just might ask the usher to move the ELMO back a bit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness NN, don't worry about that exhibit right now. But, Witness NN, are you a Bosnian Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And until approximately the 12th of June, 1993, did you live in the village of Tulica in the Kiseljak municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time, in June of 1993, were you a member of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me go back for one moment and take you to 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, were you a member of the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Mr. President, just for the next three or four questions concerning his background, go into private session, I believe we can get over this very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. We will now have a private session which simply means that the public doesn't hear the questions and the answers that are being asked now because these are questions which relate to information which has to remain confidential. Proceed please. (Private session).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Public session).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness NN, in your own words, can you tell the Judges exactly what happened to you commencing with your arrest in 1992 and, again, take us through the events that took place in Tulica on the 12th of June of 1993, and then what happened to you once you got to the Kiseljak barracks and were held captive there for just short of one week; in your own words, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I was first arrested in Busovaca, I was a member of the Patriotic League and I was stationed in Kiseljak. And because I was not going back to Tulica during a period of time, Nail Fazlibacic, Muhadis Tulic, and I went home to -- for a change of clothes and to take a proper bath. As we were coming back, near the village of Lepenica, we tried to hitchhike back to Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness NN, what time frame is this, if you could tell the Judges? Could you put an approximate time and date on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was sometime around the end of July and in early August, as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. And at Han Ploca, a barricade had been erected by the TO, that is the BiH army, and we could not proceed along that road in a vehicle, so we waited there to see what would happen next. And then Mato Lucic called Maturice arrived at about dusk, and someone whose name I cannot recall from Brnaci, his nickname was Crnogorac, in a red Golf. And then they talked with Sead Sinanbasic and reached an agreement. Mr. Sinanbasic was commander of the TO at the time, and they agreed that this checkpoint would be removed so that there would be free movement of traffic and no problems and this was done. On the way to Kiseljak, in the village of Brnaci, we were arrested, but before that another vehicle came and Mato Lucic, Maturice, and Crnogorac from Brnaci were in it and they passed us as we were making our way towards Kiseljak. As we were approaching Brnaci we were stopped and simply we were arrested, we were made to get out of the vehicle, our weapons were taken away and we were placed in a van without windows. There was a small window in the back of this van. Through it, I could see that from the social hall in Brnaci, the social hall building in Brnaci, Sead Sinanbasic and Nusret Masin were being led out. There were a number of HVO soldiers around and you could see voices -- raised voices, and then they took us via Busovaca, that means all the around, a roundabout way to Kresevo and then to Kiseljak, to the barracks there. When they brought us to the Kiseljak barracks, we also observed a lot of HVO soldiers, and I cannot tell exactly how much time we spent there at the barracks. And then we were driven to the town of Busovaca. They brought us in front of the police station building in Busovaca and, again, they searched us, they removed our belts and our shoelaces. They also removed the TO insignia and they pulled off the badges, amulets that we had around our necks and then eventually we were taken to the cells. There were seven of us who were brought there and we were all placed in the same cell, that is, during those two or three days that we spent there. Only if the policeman on duty let us, we were allowed to go to the toilet or have a drink of water and freshen up. And as far as food is concerned, we did not eat anything during that time. And we were mentally abused, we were cursed, they cursed us, "Balija's mother" and things like that throughout this period. In the end, and this is four or five days later, a policeman came. His nickname was Isus or Jesus and he asked: "Are there any volunteers." Nail Fazlibacic and I stepped forward. Then when we came out, they took off the handcuffs which had been placed on us, and he said that there would be some work for us to do. A truck had been brought there packed with -- loaded with tobacco, so we were unloading this tobacco and taking it into the building of the police station. After that, we were taken back to the police station where we were handcuffed again, immediately with hands behind our backs and were left there together -- to be together with those who had stayed there. Again, there was some conflict around Kacuni and Busovaca. This is what we heard, because the people were talking in these hallways, so we could hear it. And then I don't know who of the policemen who were there said this, but he threatened us. He said: "You see, our troops are advancing towards Kacuni and should anything happen to any one of us, you all will be killed." While we were there, Sead Sinanbasic told us that Ivica Rajic had already threatened him before with arrest if he did not do as he wanted, that is, Mr. Rajic wanted. On the fourth or fifth day, we were taken out to be interrogated. Every one of us went there by himself and the interrogation was conducted by certain Vlado, whom I don't know, but when I was being taken back from the interrogation, Ahmed Hatic told me that they had known each other before and that Vlado used to be with Gravjinicic (phoen). During the interrogation with Vlado, I was not physically mistreated, just the documents that I had, I mean, I had an ID card, a personal ID card, I had a phone book. He asked questions related to that. He wanted to know certain addresses. He said: "It's lucky that your RPG is clean," meaning I did not shoot from it and I did not kill anyone. After that, everything was regular. We were given two meals a day, and Ahmed Hatic and Mufid Tulic, Nusef Masi and I were exchanged; that is, we were taken back to the town of Kiseljak. After that, my Patriotic League unit was transferred to Mount Igman. I spent about two months up there and, after those two months, I went back to my village of Tulica. I don't know how much time I spent at Tulica. And following that, I went to the village of Koscan where the BiH army had frontline positions. During this period of time which I spent in the village of Tulica, there were also some frictions and the checkpoints were erected. There were some looting of the weekend houses and some confiscating of vehicles on the part of the HVO members. When I went to the frontline at Koscan, at Igman, I spent several weeks there before the event in Tulica. On that day, I was with Mufid Bajraktarevic, and Mufid Tulic. We passed between the lines held by the HVO and the Chetniks respectively to go down to the village because we could not take any other road, everything else had been blocked. Midway through the village, we were stopped by Mediha Huseinovic and Hamdija Tulic, and they told us not to go further, not to carry our weapons there. My house is at the other end of the village. So that the Chetniks would not spot us from the Ostrik hill, and so that they wouldn't shoot, which is what they were in the habit of doing at the civilians if they saw someone carrying weapons. So we left our weapons in the house of Mediha Huseinovic, and I went to the end -- and I started towards the end of the village. When I came to Audo Huseinovic's house, humanitarian aid was being distributed there. I found my father there, and I went home together with him. I don't know exactly how long, but it could have been about an hour or two that I spent in the house and Mufid Tulic and Sakib Barjaktarevic came and asked me whether I wanted to buy some cigarettes because at that time, there was a big -- a great crisis and he had a neighbour who was a Croat and who was going to sell him these cigarettes. During this conversation, the first shell fell just above my house, so we sought shelter in my basement immediately. Rasim Huseinovic came, Ramiza Huseinovic, Hakif Huseinovic came also to hide from the shelling because they were working out in the fields. The shelling stopped for awhile and the people had grown accustomed to the shelling because it wasn't the first time and they thought it wouldn't be repeated. Sakib went to buy those cigarettes that I had just mentioned and we stayed on in the basement. Shortly after that, the shelling resumed. As far as I was able to see, it was mostly coming from the area of Vela, Buhotine, and after that, there were more shells coming from Cuvram and Voleak. These were HVO positions. I realised that something was seriously wrong, and the shelling was focused on the upper part of the village. As my father could not stay on, he was impatient. He wanted to see how the livestock and the stables were doing, and going back, when he came back, he told Mufid Tulic, that his father had run off in the direction of Lepenice, and that he was holding onto his stomach with his hand pressed against it because he had been wounded. Mufid Tulic stayed for maybe another 15 minutes or so. The shelling continued. It was gaining in intensity, and he saw smoke so he went to check whether it was his house that was on fire. As he left towards his house, I told him to take both his own weapon and my own and as soon as this stopped, I said that we would go back to the front. As my father opened the door and he saw some houses burning already in the upper part of the village, so he went to put out the fire, something that he had done before, that is, helping other people to do the same. A little while later, he came back, in great haste, to inform all of us who were there in my house that we should run for our lives because soldiers had come in, they were burning things, and that they had fired at him. There was panic. I ran to get my weapon where I had left it; however, near Audo Huseinovic's house, I noticed three soldiers heading towards me. As soon as they noticed me, they started shouting, "stop, surrender, and I had the good luck that there was a bend in the road there, so they didn't hit me when I started to run. I ran, though I didn't really know who was attacking or what for, so I ran towards Lepenice jumping over a fence, and I was tired and I felt something warm below my knee and I thought I had been hit. I reached Hasid Zahid's house, and I sat down to rest and to check to see whether I had really been wounded. That was when I heard a large group of people shouting, roughly near Djemail Huseinovic's house, and Mujo Barjaktarevic's, so I headed towards them and at Rasim Hasic's house and his barn, a soldier came out, a soldier from Brnjaci with whom I had had coffee a few months before in Kiseljak, an HVO soldier. His father used to work with me and he captured me, told me to put my hands up, to lie down. I had knapsack on me with some canned food and some bread, and he asked me straight away, what my position on the front was. And he brought me to this large group of women, children and men that had already been rounded up. Just before I was captured, as I was going from Zijad Hasic's to Rasim Hasic's house, I saw Mufid Tulic running towards Humar Rijac's (phoen) house, and when they brought me among those women and children, a little later, they also brought Mufid Tulic. They kept bringing in men from all sides, and that was when I saw that they were HVO soldiers, that they were mostly locals from Brnjaci, many of whom I recognised and I was a colleague of theirs. We had worked together. Nearby, Zijad Huseinovic's house was burning, and before that, there were people who had put the fire out, and they were trying to put out the fire on this occasion too and that was when they were arrested. After that, from the direction of Ostrik, I saw a group coming. At the beginning of the war, they called themselves Vrazija Divizija, or the Devil's division. I personally recognised among the group, Tibor Prajo, Mihilovic Drako (phoen), known as Pijuk. Tibor Prajo came up to me and asked, "What are you doing here"? I told him that this was my village and that it was where I lived. Then he asked me about Katkic Selver, Katkic. When I told him where Selver Katkic was, I asked him to help me. He just said that there was nothing he could do to help and just then, an HVO soldier who was carrying a TV set, a video recorder in a wheelbarrow, and a stereo set, and he had put on a new jacket owned by my friend, and he just waved and I saw them going off in the direction of Lepenice. Pijuk approached the group, he had a sock over his face, and he started cursing our Balija mothers, saying, you wanted a Dzamahirija, where is your Sefer and your Alija to help you now? And Salko Barjaktarevic came up then and he addressed himself to Pijuk and said, for God's sake, what are you doing? Because most of the old part of the village was already on fire and the women and children were crying. There was a lot of panic. He just answered, "Keep quiet, you old man, I'll kill you." And he actually did so. He fired two shots at him in front of all of us, and there were 70 or 80 of us there, because they kept bringing more in, and he fired these two shots into his chest. When Salko fell, in a heap, but he was still alive, then he fired another shot into his back. A little while after that, Vlatko Trogrlic known as Zuna from Lepenice came up and Zeljo Gutlilovic, known as Zara, from Kulis and another HVO soldier called Musa, nicknamed Musa, I don't exactly remember his name, they were the bodyguard of Trogrlic Vlatko, known as Zuna, and they were issuing orders to Pijuk. Pijuk came back and he separated all the able-bodied men of military age. Once he had separated us, he said, "Say goodbye to your family because you will never see them again. I'm taking you to Ostrik so you can see what the Chetniks are doing." Before taking us in the direction of Ostrik, I personally saw Anto Cuijanovic, known as Tana, coming up, and as he was a colleague from work of Zijad Huseinovic, the latter asked him if he could get some things for his two or three-month old baby, but this one wouldn't let him do that. They took us then in the direction of Ostrik, as far as the cemetary there. When we got there, he ordered us to turn around and face Kulis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "he," who is he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pujik, I'm implying Pujik. He ordered us to face Kulis and to close our ranks. While walking towards the cemetary, there were 20 or so, I don't know the exact number, of HVO soldiers with their rifles pointed at us, behind us, so there wasn't a chance of any one of us trying to flee or anything like that. When he told us to close our ranks, he took out Ahmed Barjaktarevic from the line, Mufid Tulic, Huseinovic Refik and Safet Katkic, and not far from us, maybe some 15 or 20 metres away, he and another two or three of them, I don't know the exact number, asking them about weapons, whether they had any, where they were, and so on. They hit them with their rifles and they forced them down a slope leading down from the road. Because the inclination was very steep, I couldn't see where they were going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness NN, could you tell the judges who was doing the forcing and who was being forced down the incline?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pijuk and the other HVO soldiers were forcing Safet Katkic, Huseinovic Ferid Refik and Mufid Tulic, and Ahmed Barjaktarevic down the slope. After that, I just heard bursts of fire. After that, Pijuk and the rest of them came back to the spot where all of us were lined up and he took out Halil. He was from Blazuj, a refugee, so he hit him on his shoulder. He had a long leather jacket on him, and Pijuk hit him on the shoulder and ordered him to tell who were the people that were armed and that had weapons. Halil gave the names of Zijad Huseinovic. Pijuk asked who he was and told him to come out of the line immediately. When Zijad Huseinovic had come out of the line, he was going to the spot where the others had been, maybe some ten metres away, and then Halil also called out the name of Aziz Huseinovic, Admir Barjaktarevic, but Admir Barjaktarevic didn't seem to be there when Pijuk called out his name. Aziz Huseinovic said that he didn't have any weapons, and as far as I was able to see, there was Mario Bradara known as Crnogorac, a Montenegrin, and the others that were there behind us. Mario Bradara fired two shots, as far as I remember, into Aziz Huseinovic, just below the knee into his leg, and he fell immediately to the ground. Zijad Huseinovic had been killed in the meantime. Aziz Huseinovic, when he fell to the ground, the HVO soldiers approached and kicked him, ordering him to get up. He got up and they told him, "Go over there," and he went on hopping on one leg. After that, Pijuk came up to me and Elvir Huseinovic, known as Buco, if I remember well, so he took him and me out of the line, only he hit me in the back with a rifle butt telling me to come out of the line. I passed by Zijad Huseinovic on the road and I saw Aziz Huseinovic taking off his red T-shirt and wrapping it around his leg. Pijuk then said to him, "Don't bother; you won't need it." Pijuk demanded us to produce weapons, me and Elvir Huseinovic, known as Buco, and this young man was maybe 15 years old, so he didn't have any weapons. I don't know how it happened that he ordered us to go back into line. Aziz Huseinovic was left there propped up on his arms, crying. Pijuk and the group stayed behind and we were taken towards Lepenice. They stopped us at Ibrahim Jahic's house. And a vehicle from the public utility company of Kiseljak was waiting there for us. We all had to board this truck and we were driven off in the direction of Lepenica. During the ride to Lepenica, Jahic Ibrahim threw out something wrapped in paper and he threw it into the bushes by the road. When we reached the centre of Lepenica, Milo Simic (phonetic) or Dragan or something like that was the owner of a cafe called Fortuna, that is where we stopped. I can't remember exactly who it was that ordered Ibrahim Jahic because we were being followed by a vehicle with HVO soldiers in it. They were shooting into the air to frighten us as we reached Lepenica, and I can't remember exactly who it was that told Ibrahim Jahic to get off this truck and they asked him, "Tell us, old man, what it is that you threw away?" Then, two or three HVO soldiers started beating him there. They pushed him into a car and we could see that he was being driven back towards Tulica. While in the centre of Lepenica, we saw a large number of HVO troops gathered there. And after that, they drove us in the direction of Kiseljak. On the way there, again, there were vehicles escorting us, behind us, and they were also shooting into the air to frighten us, and they drove us to the Kiseljak

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we got there, we stopped in front of the military police building and we were ordered to go inside into the corridor. All of us were lined up and I could see that prisoners were coming out of the other premises, people I knew well from Visnjica, Gomionica and Rotilj. And then several people from my village went inside to give their particulars, and then an HVO soldier came up to me with a patch over his eye and he told me to come forward. When I reached him, he took me towards the exit of the military police building, and there was a black chair there, so I sat on it. That was when I saw Mario Bradara, called Crnogorac, and he started questioning me about Alex Bahic and his whereabouts. He ordered, "Get up, sit down, get up, sit down." He cursed my Balija mother, and when I got tired, when I couldn't keep getting up, I remained seated and then he kicked me in the head and I fell. Then he ordered me to sit again on the chair and he ordered me to do push-ups. I started doing them. I maybe managed to do two or three, and then the HVO soldier with a patch on his eye started kicking me in the kidney area, the stomach and the head. Then Mario Bradara ordered me to sit on the chair again, and a small child was passing by there through the building, through the barracks, and Mario Bradara called the little boy over and told the child to hit me with his fingers. I couldn't stand it anymore. I started crying, and then Mario Bradara told me to go back, to go back into the corridor to line up with the others. When I joined the others, Selver Bajraktarevic asked where the toilet was. Then the HVO soldier with the bandage on his eye took him to show him where the toilet was. A little while after that, he returned. His nose was bloody. There was a cut across his lips. His eye was swollen and he lined up with us, with the rest of us. While we were giving our particulars, Marinko Steko was sitting there, somebody I knew well already who was, as far as I remember, an HVO police commander. As he knew me well, there was no need for me to tell him anything about myself. He knew everything about me. He just asked me why I had nothing on above the waist. I hadn't had time to put anything on. And he ordered me to join the others who were already in the corridor. Then they put us up in a room where we were incarcerated at the end of the building and while entering this room, Tica Haro from Lepenica was already detained there. Inside the room, there was nothing, just the bare floor. There were no beds or anything like that. And while standing there, during my stay there, Hemdo Bajraktarevic was taken away, and he, too, was beaten up. Also while I was there, some other people were being brought there, people whom I did not know, and they were brought there by the HVO soldiers. How shall I put it, I couldn't even tell where all the blood was coming from. They were all beaten up and they were there for maybe no longer than an hour. The policeman would again come for them and they would take them someplace and then the Red Cross came to visit us. I don't know who these people were and what they were, but they registered us. They took down the number of us who were there. After that, myself and the other people were taken to dig trenches. I was familiar with that area, so I know that we passed through the village of Gominica, and as far as I can recall, I think it was also the village of Stoikvic (phonetic) or something like that, that was the name. And this is where we dug trenches. In any event, I know very well that from that position, I think you can see the airport at Liesh (phonetic), I believe it's called. I spent two days there digging and on the second day of this labour, Vlatko Trogrlic came, as far as I recall, and he brought with him a piece of paper with a list, a list of people for the exchange. My name was also on that list. There were all together ten of us. We were taken back to the barracks and there was a red mini bus in which we were taken to the village of Lepenica. I recognised Marinko Steko and the others there in Lepenice, both the HVO and the policeman. I can't recall all those names, though, now. And we were taken directly to Gojakovac, to the house of Mirko Jendo, and that's where the exchange took place. We crossed over into the territory of the BiH army, and I then came to the village of Zabrde. Two or three days later, I joined the defence at the Koscan line and while I was there at this frontline, we could both see and hear quite well that there were our prisoners being kept there and being forced to dig trenches and fox holes. As a corroboration of what I say that there were prisoners there on the frontline digging trenches, I can say that Vinko Katava from the village of Kulijes called out, he said -- and told him that Hilmo Jahic was there and Bajro Bajmaktarevic. He was an aging man, 65 to 70 years, old who was released by the HVO soldiers without any exchange. They simply let him cross over to our territory. After that, I was redeployed to the frontline at Golubac. And also during a sabotage operation, a special operation by the BiH army, I don't know the exact number of people who had been taken prisoners, but these were our own people who were imprisoned by the HVO and who dug trenches for them. I can only remember the name of Esad Naradil (phonetic). So I spent that entire time on those frontlines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Witness NN, you have just about told all the events to which you were a witness. Perhaps the Prosecutor has some clarifications he would like to ask in order to put some order back to add some dates. Perhaps you would rather do this after the break. That might, in fact, be better.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I do believe that that would be better, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We're going to suspend for about 20 minutes. The hearing is suspended.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is now resumed. Have the accused brought in, please. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, thank you. If I can move into the followup questions at this juncture, I believe we can move through this rapidly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness NN, I'm going to ask you a few questions about the testimony that you just gave to the Court, and I want to start with the period of time that you were held in jail in Busovaca. During that period of time, did Dario Kordic come to the prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Dario Kordic did come to the prison, and when he came, one of the policemen who were guarding us there said, "Get out. Get out, the gentlemen are arriving." We immediately stepped out of our cells into the hallway. We were lined up there and Dario Kordic came in with two of his bodyguards. And I knew him from before when I was working for the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you knew Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphones, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw Dario Kordic in the jail in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the HVO military police and the civilian police working together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in this prison where we were, as far as I remember, this was a civilian police prison and also the civilian police precinct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me turn, Witness NN, to your arrest and also the conversations that took place at the checkpoint in Han Ploca. I thought you said the latter part of July, early part of August in 1992, and you identified an individual by the name of Mato Lucic, also known as Maturice as being there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can request the assistance of the Usher at this point, and if we can move to the first three photographs that are on the table with the witness, and for reference point, Mr. President, Your Honours, these are stills that were taken from Exhibit 260. If I can have the first number. Starting with Exhibit 337, if we can put that on the ELMO. Witness NN, do you recognise that man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Mato Lucic called Maturice from the village of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn to the next photograph, 338. Witness NN, do you recognise those three men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is Mato Lucic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you take the pointer and point to them, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mato Lucic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the man in the middle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ivica Rajic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know the one on the left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It's Hravoja Kristic, a baker from Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are the individuals that were part of the special unit behind them in the background?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the background, yes, and behind them, maybe some others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn to the third photograph, 339. Again, can you identify those individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know this elderly man only by his nickname which is Bojo, and he is from Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're pointing to the elderly man at the podium?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ivica Rajic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's on the left-hand side of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Right next to him is Mato Lucic, called Maturice. And behind the old Bojo is Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness NN, Mato Lucic, are you aware of the units that he commanded?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly which units, but all three of them, whom I pointed out, with the exception of the old Bojo, is the commanding group which was in the Kiseljak barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us move to the next photograph, exhibit 340. Now, during the course of your testimony concerning the attack on Tulica, you mentioned an individual that you knew as Pijuk. Is Pijuk in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point to him?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to request that out of the entire group seen on this photograph, two persons were circled and we don't know by whom, because if this photograph is to be used for identification, I believe that we shouldn't premark it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think the Prosecutor must have put the circles on. I suppose so, or the Office of the Prosecutor. It doesn't seem to be a basic problem to me, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I don't know, but in a system where multiple persons are identified in a photograph, you do not premark them. You have the witness identify them one by one and only then mark them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, no, I can't accept this comment. Since the 23rd of June, we've been looking at things with arrows and an notations and other things. I can't sustain that objection. The Office of the Prosecutor identified in order to facilitate the dialogue between himself and the witness. Let's not spend too much time on these issues, Mr. Kehoe. There are two people that were circled. One has a 1 and one has a 2. Witness NN, what is the name of the person whose face is marked with the circle and the number 1; is that Pijuk?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is Zoravko Mihajlovic called Pijuk who was in the village of Tulica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you pointing to the individual with the number 2 next to him or the number 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My apologies, the person number 2 is Zoravko Mihjlovic called Pijuk whom I knew well from before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe the President asked you about the individual whose circled with the number 1. Do you see that individual?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do see this person, and it is Mario Bradara, and as far as I know, his nickname is Crnogorac or "Montenegrin", and he took part in the attack on Tulica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Okay. Number 1 is Bradara and Pijuk is number 2. Let's move to the next photograph, please, 341.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might ask one followup question concerning that photograph. He's called the Montenegrin, does that mean that Mario Bradara was from Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. In Bosnia, this would be a nickname typical for people who are well-built, tall and strong, as far as I know, and also who are dark-haired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I don't think it's essential for this trial to simply-- we'll simply say that, all right, if you're in good health, they can call you Montenegrin. Let's move on to the next photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one further question on Exhibit 340. The individuals that are on the right of this photograph, on the other side of Pijuk, do you know who those individuals were or what unit they were part of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These were persons who were from the Brnjaci and Kiseljak general area. They were all members of the HVO. There are persons here who are from Lepenica, but most of these persons I know pretty well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they part of the special units within the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us move to the next photograph, 341.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me, just what do you call special units of the HVO. You ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Witness NN, could you explain that for Judge Riad, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: What is a special unit of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, these were sabotage units which would only be engaged in attacks and things like that. In other words, they are not soldiers who are used to uphold the frontline positions, so these are sabotage units who conduct sabotage actions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Sabotage actions where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Wherever their command sends them, wherever they're ordered to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: In the frontline or in cities? Can you be more clear about the sabotage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at the frontlines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness NN, were these sabotage units used in the attack on Tulica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the way, Witness NN, what was the day of the attack on Tulica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Tulica was attacked on 12 June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could move to the next photograph, 341. Who is that? Who is in the circle there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The person circled here is Zoravko Mihjlovic also known as Pijuk, whom I had known before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move to 342. Witness NN, do you recognise the individual whose head is circled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise him. This is Tibor Prajo who was the HVO soldier and who approached me directly during the attack at Tulica and asked me: What are you doing here? He asked me of Safet Katkic, where he was and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness NN, is this the individual that you asked for help?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, this is the person that I asked for help and who told me just that he couldn't do anything for me to help. When I saw him that day, he was stripped to waist and had bandoleers over his bare chest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you whether or not he was running the attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us move to the next photograph, 343.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Repeat your question, please, I don't think the microphone was on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. Let us turn to Exhibit 343 and I direct your attention to the man whose head is circled.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This person also took part in the attack on Tulica. He lives in the village of Brnjaci and he was carrying two rifles, one in the front, one in the back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn to the next exhibit, Exhibit 344. Do you recognise the individual that is in Exhibit 344?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He also took part in the attack on Tulica, and his father worked in the same company where I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were all these individuals that you mentioned as being in the attack on Tulica, were they all members of the HVO, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were all members and soldiers of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the individuals that you identified as part of the Devil's Division, was the Devil's Division part of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is, except that it is another sabotage unit, and this is what they called themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can turn to the next exhibit which is an exhibit of the confrontation lines. Mr. Dubuisson, I believe we're finished with the photographs. Just the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUBUISSON
utterances.text: This is 345.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can put that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness NN, this is a map of the confrontation lines that was prepared with your assistance; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the confrontation lines, the red is the Bosnian-Serb area, the blue is the HVO area, and the green is the area controlled by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you, using the pointer, just point out the village of Tulica on the map, Exhibit 345?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating) it's right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what is the approximate date of these lines or were these the approximate lines on the 12th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not have big trenches and complete fortifications on that 12th of June when the attack on Tulica took place. Ten or fifteen days later, everything was dug through and there were complete trenches and fortifications made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were these the approximate lines of confrontation on the 12th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned during your testimony the location of Ostrik and that is colored in red. Do you see that, sir, and can you point to that on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that high ground controlled by the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next to that, there is high ground in blue with the name Plesevac under it. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is here. (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that controlled by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, for awhile, it was -- it changed hands. It was under the control of the HVO and then the army of the Republic Serbska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this particular area, Witness NN, did the Bosnian Serbs and the HVO meet with one another and speak with one another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn our attention to the next map, Mr. Dubuisson, if we could, and I would like to ask you several questions, Witness NN, about the actual attack on Tulica on the 12th of June, 1993. And if we could put this exhibit, and is that 346?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUBUISSON
utterances.text: That's right, 346.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, excuse me, your question when you asked if the Serbs spoke to the Croats, if the Bosnian Serbs spoke to the Croats, could you explain for what purpose?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness NN, could you explain and answer Judge Riad's question as to the purpose of the HVO speaking to the Bosnian Serbs in this location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that location, the lines were merged and there you had contraband being smuggled across, cigarettes and liquor, and before the attack on Tulica, they had contacts. They were in contact, let's say, at Kobiljaca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Was this contact related to the attack on Tulica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't believe so. I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned, Witness NN, that on the 12th of June, there was shelling into the village of Tulica, and you gave various locations where the shelling had come from; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this shelling come from both Bosnian Serb controlled areas and HVO-controlled areas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn our attention to the map that's on the ELMO, Exhibit 346, and, again, with your assistance, this map was prepared with various arrows and spots where detonations were fired from; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, the red area is the Bosnian Serb area and the blue area is the HVO area; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do the various detonation areas and the arrows, are those the places where you indicated that the shelling came from on the right-hand side from the Bosnian Serb positions and on the left-hand side from the HVO positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just look at this map a little more closely around the village of Tulica, and can you point -- do you see the semi-circle around the village of Tulica in black? Can you point to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that designate, that line, that semi-circle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To me, it would signify that we were encircled, that nobody could get out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness NN, can you explain to the Judges how the attack took place and the role played by the HVO soldiers and the role played by the sabotage units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The HVO soldiers had the role in the sense that they were deployed in this semi-circle here, and the sabotage units entered from the direction of Ostrik and between the villages of Bombarda and Kulis, and the only space open where you could flee was in the direction of the Bosnian Serb army, Bilalovac, everything else was sealed, everything else was surrounded, because whoever tried to flee in the direction of Kulis or Lepenica were brought to this place where Salko Bajraktarevic was later killed where all these civilians and women and children were being collected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the village of Tulica, is the village of Tulica a Muslim village, a Croat village, or is it mixed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The village of Tulica is a Muslim village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately how many people lived in Tulica and approximately how many houses were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'd say about a hundred homes. My best recollection would be somewhere between 4- and 500 persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you noted that the upper part of the village was shelled the heaviest; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were houses burned in the upper part of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the lower part of the village burned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what ultimately happened after the Muslims were expelled from Tulica to the homes in the lower part of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, most of the homes were looted and a number of houses in the lower part of Tulica was used to provide accommodation for the Croat refugees from the areas around Vares and elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you some questions about the attack itself. The HVO soldiers that came into the attack, did you see them wearing any type of ribbon or designation and what was the color of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they wore the HVO insignia here on the uniforms, and they also wore white ribbons in order to be recognised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You noted during the course of your testimony that you recognised an individual, an HVO commander, by the name of Trogrlic, also known as Zuna; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was a commander of the Lepenica area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, based on what you saw, Witness NN, do you know whether or not he was commanding this attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could infer that he was a commander in charge of this attack because this man, Vlatko Trogrlic called Zuna and Anto Cuijanovic, who was a commander at Brnjaci, as well as Pijuk, they were all there at Tulica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you noted previously that people were giving orders to Pijuk; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see who that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did see. It was Vlatko Trogrlic called Zuna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn to Pijuk himself. The individual you named as Pijuk, did he attend to indicate to you that he was a Bosnian Serb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he told us when he arrived there to this crowd. He said, "I'm taking you away, so say goodbye to your own, and you'll see what the Serbs are doing. You'll never see them again."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why do you think he did that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did that so that we should think that the Serbs had got into the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was it clear to you that the HVO units that were commanded by Zuna and the men that were with Pijuk were working together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. These were all HVO soldiers, only they were local commanders, as I have mentioned already, Vlatko Trogrlic known as Zuna, Anto Cuijanovic known as Tana and the others. And I knew all of these very well from before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me talk to you about some of the victims that were murdered during that day, and I believe we start with Bajaktarevic Salko. And I want to ask you how old Salko Bajaktarevic was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was between 65 and 70, something like that, Salko Bajaktarevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Salko Bajaktarevic, a Bosnian Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the next four that were murdered were Bajaktarevic Ahmed, Tulic Mufid, Huseinovic Refic, also known as Ferid, Katkic Safet; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they all Bosnian Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they were killed, were they making any attempt at all to escape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I couldn't see that, because it was very steep. They were down the slope.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they pushed down that slope?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who pushed them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pijuk and the other two or three who were with him, they were pushing them with their rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you noted during your testimony that you didn't actually see these four individuals shot, but you heard the gunfire; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever seen these four individuals alive again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you next mentioned another two individuals, the first one being Huseinovic Zijad?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a Bosnian Muslim man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe you observed him dead on the ground; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during the course of your testimony, I'm not sure if you mentioned this individual or not, but during the events in Tulica that we have been discussing, was an individual by the name of Huseinovic Kasim brought before the group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Huseinovic Kazim, he came from the direction of Lepenica. He was brought there just after us to the spot where we were. When they brought him there, Pijuk asked, "who is this man?" One of the soldiers told him that he had already admitted that he had a rifle at home and that they had brought him to take the rifle from him. Pijuk just asked where his house was and when Kazim answered, he said, "Fine, we've found it." Then a group of HVO soldiers who were there behind our backs, they started beating Kazim. The man was screaming. When they took him to the same spot where they had executed those other people, I saw a part of his head had been cracked open and that something was coming out of it. The man was letting out unheard of cries, and then Pijuk and this group with him killed him immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, Huseinovic Kazim was a Bosnian Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Zijad Huseinovic was a Bosnian Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also talked about Huseinovic Aziz, was he a Bosnian Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see any of those men alive again after that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after the killing of Kasim Huseinovic, did someone give an order to Pijuk to stop killing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I personally cannot recall, but others were saying that somebody had said, that's enough killing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't know who that was; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after you were taken from the area, you mentioned that you were put on a truck and you were taken towards Lepenica, and an individual by the name of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And an individual by the name of Jahic Ibrahim through something out of the truck; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old is Ibrahim Jahic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between 55 and 60.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he was taken out of the truck and brought back towards the direction of Tulica, after that time, have you ever seen Ibrahim Jahic again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Nobody knows anything about him or Fatima Huseinovic to this day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I can move -- at this point, you were taken to the Kiseljak barracks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this point, you were taken to the Kiseljak barracks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were taken there, but I had been to the Kiseljak barracks from before so I know well the outlay of the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may turn to the next exhibit, which is the exhibit which is an enlargement of exhibit 75, and if I might have a number, Mr. Dubuisson, on this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUBUISSON
utterances.text: This is 347.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: The witness mentioned Fatima Huseinovic. This is the first time she's mentioned, and he never mentioned any women in this whole operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness NN, you were present during the individuals that were shot that you testified of. Did you have information that other people were killed in the village on that day, including Fatima Huseinovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Fatima Huseinovic was killed on that very day. Safija Tulic, and I can't remember another woman by the name of Tulic, three of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But why were women killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They tried to escape towards Kulis, so that the soldiers who were there, they killed them because there was a lot of shooting. There were soldiers all around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these Bosnian Muslim women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how old they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Safija Tulic, as far as I know, was about 60 to 65. Her younger daughter-in-law was about 45 to 50, and Fatima Tulic, she was also around -- no, sorry, Fatima Huseinovic, she was around 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: May I proceed, Judge Riad? If we can move to the exhibit that is on the map, exhibit 347, and the first question, Mr. President, if we can just go into private session for this one question, and then we can come out of private session after this one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Private session for a single question then. (In private session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (In public session)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to this particular exhibit, there are two numbers that are listed there, number 2 and number 3. Can you tell the judges exactly what is designated number 2 and number 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 2 is where the command staff were, the command forces, the HVO command. Number 3 designates two buildings of which I'm not sure which one I was incarcerated in, whether it was in the first or the second, but one of the two, that is for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness NN, were all the individuals that were incarcerated in those buildings when you got there on the 16th of June, 1993 and until you left, were they all Bosnian Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned during the course of your testimony several individuals who had been severely beaten, one of which was beaten beyond -- you didn't know where the blood was coming from; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, not one of them, but three.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned a visit to the Kiseljak barracks by the Red Cross; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these individuals removed from the barracks prior to the visit by the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They were removed before the Red Cross arrived, and as far as I can remember, a military policeman in person came for them. I remember well his name. His name was Pero. He had a mustache and he's from Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you also mentioned that when you came to the Kiseljak barracks on the 16th of June, 1993, you were beaten by Crnogorac, and an HVO soldier with a plaster patch on his eye; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, only there's a small error. It was not on the 16th of June, but on the 12th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, the 12th of June. And you have identified Crnogorac as Mario Bradara?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the same individual that had been part of the attack back in Tulica earlier that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn, if we can, to exhibit -- Mr. Dubuisson, would this be 348, the map with the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DUBUISSON
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn to exhibit 348, if we can put that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at exhibit 348, and there are various villages marked in yellow, Witness NN, and then an area that is designated in orange; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that area in orange marked with your assistance, and, if so, what does it reflect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These are the villages Rotilj, Visnijica, Polje Visnijica, Gromiljak, Gomionica, Suinjarevo. These are Muslim villages which had already been attacked before we were incarcerated in the Kiseljak barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, during the course of your testimony, you mentioned that you were taken to dig trenches. Is the approximate location of where you were taken to dig trenches marked on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're pointing to the area that is marked in orange; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I know this very well because we were driven through Kiseljak to the village of Gomionica. We passed the village, and at the end of the village, there is a valley, a vale, and then we went from there on foot because you couldn't drive any further, and I don't know the exact name of that village up there, but that is where we dug trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness NN, you also mentioned that after you were released and then you went back to the line in Koscan, that you heard additional digging of trenches taking place across the line on the HVO side; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this trench digging being done by Bosnian Muslim prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I turn our attention, Mr. President, to the last exhibit, and that is exhibit 349, and just for accuracy's sake, Mr. President, 349 is a reduced black and white copy of the confrontation lines, the coloured confrontation lines in exhibit 345.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn our attention, Witness NN, to exhibit 349. Again, with your assistance, was the orange marking placed on this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do the orange markings reflect? What are they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The orange markings indicate the HVO frontlines as they were then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that indicate the area where trenches were being dug?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you hear this going on when you were across the line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I could hear it, especially in this area that I'm pointing to now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're pointing to the area of Koscan; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness NN, having come from Tulica and having been close to those lines, did you believe that the HVO units in that area had a relationship with the Bosnian Serb units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, there were contacts between them. They could cross over at Koblijaca, Rakovica, Hadzici, individuals could do that. I don't know about any groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me move ahead. Did you have an opportunity or occasion to be in Mount Igman where you had encountered the defendant, Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was around 1995, 1996. I don't know. I can't place it exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this happen to be a very dangerous piece of road coming in and out of Sarajevo where the Serbs attacked this area frequently?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a period that is not covered by the indictment, so we object.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: What is quite clear, Mr. President, is that the defendant had a relationship with the Bosnian Serbs, and what this witness will designate is that in a very serious time when they were travelling down a very serious road, he observed Blaskic make a phone call and in a place where the Bosnian Serbs were routinely attacking the then federation, HVO and BiH, there was no firing at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, but I think then you haven't asked your question properly. You have to reformulate it, but we can't begin to allude to events of 1995. Either you have to modify your question or move to another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question is of the 1995 period. If, Mr. President, you don't want me to ask that question, then I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The witness said '95 or '96. '96 is two years after the end of the period in the indictment, and the inference urged by counsel, we think, is so specious that it doesn't support the inquiry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, the decision will take. Move to another question, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, if I may have one moment to consult with my colleagues. Mr. President, if I may move to admit, and I believe we started with 337 through exhibit 349 at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me. I was speaking with my colleague there and wasn't paying attention. Would you repeat what you just said, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, if I can move at this time to admit exhibits, if I may start at the outset, I believe it is, 337 through 349, the exhibits that were just discussed by Witness NN.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I had stopped at 349, yes, that was the last one, the one that's still on the ELMO; is that right, Mr. Dubuisson?

utterances.speaker: MR. DUBUISSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No objection? All right. Then these documents are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: One last exhibit, Mr. President, when most of these photographs were taken from the rally that took place in December of 1992 that was previously viewed by the Trial Chamber, one photograph was taken from the unedited version, and I've provided an unedited version to counsel, and I would like to move the unedited version in as exhibit 260C. I will tell you candidly that the unedited version has, in addition to a couple of more photographs, it has numerous standing around of soldiers, and we edited it down so we could expedite matters in the courtroom. Nevertheless, given the fact that some of these photographs that we have in evidence are based on the unedited version, I think it's encumbent upon the Prosecutor to put the unedited version in as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: No objections, subject to our review of the tape. If we review it and have an objection, we will bring it to the court and to counsel's attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's fine, Mr. President. I just wanted to cover the basis for which these photographs came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. There's no objection on the part of the Defence. Let me ask you, Mr. Kehoe, have you completed what you wanted to ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we have no further questions of Witness NN.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It's 1.00. We're going to suspend our work and we will resume on Monday morning at 10.00; is that right? Yes, 10.00 Monday morning. Court stands adjourned. We will resume at 10.00 on Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: be reconvened on Monday, the 11th day of May, 1998 at 10.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
